newsitem.title: USA: AMR, BA seek US approval of alliance.
newsitem.headline: AMR, BA seek US approval of alliance.

text.p: American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp, and British Airways said Friday they submitted a joint application to the Department of Transportation for formal U.S. approval of the alliance they had announced last June.

They said the application requested antitrust immunity for the linkup, which would permit the two carriers to coordinate their passenger and cargo activities between the United States and Europe, and to market their operations jointly.

American Airlines Chairman Robert Crandall said the British and U.S. governments have each said they want to achieve an "open skies" aviation agreement as a prerequisite to approving the alliance, and good progress had been made with British regulatory authorities toward reaching an agreement.
"Thus, this application is the logical next step in the process of securing all the needed regulatory approvals," Crandall said.

American Airlines noted in a statement that Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said it would approve the alliance if both carriers agreed to certain conditions, and the continuing U.S.-British talks suggested that a free market agreement could be achieved.
Crandall said, "An American-British Airways alliance would provide consumers with important new price, service and quality options in the global marketplace, and we're eager to move ahead."
Under the alliance, American and British Airways would also establish reciprocity between their frequent flier programs, but this does not require U.S. regulatory approval.
Crandall said that because the United States had already approved alliances between U.S. and other European airlines, "fairness requires that DoT also approve the American-BA alliance."

The alliances he referred to were the ones linking United Airlines, a unit of UAL Corp, with Lufthansa and SAS, Delta Air Lines with Belgian national airline Sabena, Swiss Air and Austrian Airlines, and Northwest Airlines with Royal Dutch KLM Airlines.

American Airlines noted that while the previous combinations of open skies agreements and alliances have the effect of reducing nonstop trans-Atlantic competition, the American-British Airways linkup would be the only such treaty to produce an actual increase in competition.

American said its linkup with British Airways would increase trans-Atlantic competition because the bilateral open skies agreement would permit every large U.S. carrier to operate from London to its U.S. hubs.
